title: Snack Stack Arcade
premise: A neon-styled arcade snack-management game where the player cycles tiny isometric stations through order deployment, charging, and jackpot cash-out to build score.
interaction_model: Single-pointer/tap input on an isometric grid with three manually selected action modes: prep, cook, and serve.
objective: Keep stations cycling efficiently through prep, timed charging, and collection to earn as much money as possible.
progression: Endless score-chasing progression with no explicit levels or ending; difficulty is mostly self-managed through juggling multiple stations on a configurable grid.
theme: Retro-futurist snack arcade with sci-fi vending/cooking machines, glowing cabinets, and prize-ticket framing.
mood: Bright, playful, energetic, arcade-like, and forgiving.
likely_audience: players who enjoy light management loops
younger audiences drawn to colorful, friendly presentation
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core three-step loop because state transitions and tutorial text are explicit in code.
High confidence that the game is score-driven and endless because only money accumulation is tracked and no end state is implemented.
Moderate confidence on genre naming because the game borrows from clicker, cooking, and light management patterns without fully matching any one genre.
recreation_prompt: Create a full-screen mobile-friendly HTML5 canvas game called "Snack Stack Arcade," presented as a neon retro-futurist arcade management toy viewed on a small isometric grid of stations. The player should use simple tap controls and three large mode buttons labeled like a playful sci-fi workflow: one mode places a fresh snack order onto any empty station, the second mode starts a timed charge/cook process on stations that already hold an order, and the third mode cashes out completed glowing stations for money. The main loop should be endless and score-focused: tap empty stations to load them, switch tools to activate processing, wait a few seconds while stations animate and show progress, then collect a fixed cash reward from finished stations and repeat across the whole grid as efficiently as possible. Use a polished arcade HUD with a money counter, tutorial hint panel, and reactive status banner, and make the visuals feel like glassy neon cabinets with bright cyan, pink, and gold accents over a dark purple space-arcade background. Render the stations in an isometric board layout on canvas, with each tile showing clear state changes such as empty prompts, loaded ingredients or payloads, charging glow and progress bars, and finished prize trays. Include juicy feedback for every action: particles, floating reward text, bounce animations, success and failure callouts, satisfying UI sounds, looping background music, and optional haptic-style feedback hooks. Wrong actions should not cause a hard fail, but they should trigger a playful error response and remind the player of the correct beam-in → charge → jackpot order. Keep the experience accessible, readable on phones, and easy to understand instantly, with the strategic depth coming from keeping as many stations active as possible at once rather than from complex upgrades or narrative.
